rows.note:
Degraded strictly precedes tripped, and one success recovers — driven over the wire rather than asserted on a struct. The lane's `r27-flaky` upstream is a shell that refuses to exec while a sentinel file exists; the ROUTER never reads that file, so nothing the router does can make this arm pass. Probe one: degraded. Probe two, at this server's own `tripAfter: 2`: tripped. The lane removes the sentinel and probes again: healthy.

The asymmetry is the design and is asserted as such. Failing takes `tripAfter` readings; recovering takes one, because reporting a working server as tripped sends somebody to debug a server that is fine. `UpstreamHealthPolicyTests` H9 additionally walks every threshold from 2 to 5 and requires degraded at each failure below it.

rows.note:
A scheduled sweep observes; it does not create the thing it is observing. `UpstreamHealthMonitorTests` H16 stages a server with a 60-second interval that the pool reports as not live, runs one sweep, and asserts on the PROBER rather than on the record: the thing that would spawn a child was never called, and the record says so with a reason rather than a failure.

That is REQ-001 stated from inside this feature — at rest there are zero child processes — and it is the whole reason background probing defaults to off as well. H11 is the other half: a decline never counts against `consecutiveFailures`, so a sweep that declines twenty-one idle servers forever cannot trip them. The witness run records the same property from outside the process: before any probe, the report is `unprobed` and `ps(1)` shows no child of the daemon.

A route that answered `declined` while spawning the child anyway would pass every status assertion above it. `disabled` means never spawned to be warmed or indexed, so a probe route that spawned one would be a hole in the switch rather than a health check.

A configured value the router will not take is REFUSED and reported, never clamped in silence. The lane's `r27-refused` server writes `tripAfter: 1` and `probeIntervalMs: 10`; the report carries both refusals with the value as written, the floor that rejected it, and a `scope` saying which block to fix, while `policy` reports the value actually in force.

The `tripAfter` floor of 2 is this item's own version of the vacuity rule: with a threshold of 1 the first failure trips, `degraded` is unreachable, and the guarantee that an upstream is flagged degraded before it is tripped would hold only because nothing can enter the state it names. rows.note:
Every CONFIGURED credential is absent from the bundle, and the document that omits it is a real one. The absence alone is the easiest unfailable assertion in this repository: it holds over an empty document, over a 404, and over a gatherer that never read the config. So it is asserted beside three things that must be PRESENT — a public canary planted in the same log line, the env key name, and the header key name — and beside `"value":"present"`, which proves a decision was taken about the value rather than the whole server having been skipped.

Layer 1 is what this case pins: an env value, a header value and a URL's userinfo are never PLACED in the document, so no key name a config invents can smuggle one through. It follows Describe's own construction, which maps the pair arrays to their keys before anything else touches them (B10).

rows.note:
Layer 2, and the channel layer 1 structurally cannot reach. A credential arrives in a diagnostics export by more routes than the field it was configured in: an upstream that rejects a call and quotes the token back in its error text, a command line carrying `--token=`, a log line somebody wrote by hand. Those are strings the bundle has every reason to carry, and the only thing distinguishing the secret inside one is its VALUE.

The scrub runs over the value tree ONCE, as the last step, so every string goes through it by construction rather than because each site remembered to call it — the property that survives the next person adding a section. Object keys are scrubbed as well as values.

`occurrencesRemoved` is asserted non-zero, because a scrubber that ran and a scrubber that had something to do read as the same clean bundle and only one of them is evidence.
rows.why: a measurement, not a task: status 'pass' may only be retirable/verified-done. It rolls up to its surface.

rows.note:
The needle floor, which is a correctness rule rather than a performance one. An env value of `1`, `true` or `dev` used as a scrub needle deletes every occurrence of that text from every log line in the bundle — the timestamps, the ports, the word `device`. The result READS as thorough redaction and is a corrupted document, and nobody looking at it can tell which.

So a value below 8 characters is not used as a needle, is named in `unscrubbable` with the reason, and is still withheld by layer 1. The assertion that bites is the positive one: `dev-server on port 3000` must survive intact.

BOTH out-of-family reviewers proposed an entropy filter on top of the floor, to stop a value like `production` scrubbing that word out of the logs. Declined, and the reason is the direction of the error: an over-redaction announces itself in place as `<redacted:MODE>` and a reader can see exactly what happened; an under-redaction is silent. A second exclusion tuned by entropy moves values from the first class to the second on a judgement nobody can audit from the bundle.
rows.why: a measurement, not a task: status 'pass' may only be retirable/verified-done. It rolls up to its surface.

rows.note:
A secret does not always reach a log line as itself. It reaches it percent-encoded when it travelled in a URL and base64-encoded when it travelled in a `Basic` credential, and a scrubber that knows only the literal reports a clean bundle over both. Both out-of-family lanes raised this independently and it is the one addition of theirs taken wholesale.

JSON escaping is DELIBERATELY NOT a third variant, and that is where this departs from both reviews. They are right that a token containing a quote appears in the SERIALISED document as `\"` and would survive a needle search over the finished bytes. The scrub does not search the finished bytes: it walks the value tree before serialisation, where every string is still unescaped. Scrubbing earlier removes the whole class rather than enumerating its members.

rows.note: N8. The inertness guard on the untrusted-input boundary, made capable of failing. M19 shipped `MarkdownSecurityTests.htmlIsInert` with four spellings that named `javascript:`, no scheme, or nothing, and two assertions -- no link, no `imageURL` -- that `MarkdownInline.sanitized` makes true of every input it touches. It could not go red. rows.note: The Windows task scheduler holding a task the product registered, read by an API that did not write it. The writer is MCPRouter.Shell.Live's LogonTaskSupervisor driving schtasks.exe with the Task Scheduler XML it builds; the recorder is Get-ScheduledTask, the ScheduledTasks module over the scheduler's WMI provider - a different API, a different process and a different vocabulary for the same facts. The XML says RunLevel LeastPrivilege and the recorder answers RunLevel Limited, and nothing in this repository translates between them. The scheduler also normalised the interval this run asked for, PT60S, into PT1M, which is the plainest available evidence that the read did not come back through anything this code wrote. EIGHT ARMS, AND TWO ARE ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT. BASELINE requires the recorder to report the task ABSENT before registration - without it, a task left behind by an interrupted run makes every other arm pass over a run that registered nothing. SILENCE requires it to report absence again after removal, which is what separates a reader from an echo: a recorder that always answered yes would satisfy the six product arms by construction. The other six read the three claims LifecyclePresentation prints to the operator - triggered at logon, un-elevated, restarting on failure - plus the executable and port this run asked for, plus presence and removal. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and the reason it is one case rather than the whole of REQ-035: nothing here logs the user out, so the trigger has never been watched to fire, and nothing here starts or kills a daemon, so the restart has never been watched to happen. DEF-081 carries those two. This case settles that the registration the product performs produces, in the Windows task scheduler, a task carrying the properties the product's own UI describes - which before 2026-09-02 was unmeasured entirely, and which DEF-074 recorded as a supervision model nothing performed.
rows.why: a measurement, not a task: status 'pass' may only be retirable/verified-done. It rolls up to DEF-074, DEF-081.

rows.note: The COM activator the Windows notification platform wrote, read out of the registry by a process that did not write it. The writer is AppNotificationManager.Register() inside the shell; the recorder is HKCU through PowerShell's registry provider, and nothing of this repository's sits between them. Four arms. BASELINE requires the AUMID key to be ABSENT before the shell launches, so what the other three read is this launch. The three EFFECT arms read the key, the CustomActivator CLSID it names, and that CLSID's LocalServer32 - which came back as MCPRouter.Shell.exe carrying the platform's own ----AppNotificationActivated: argument, a string this repository does not write anywhere. THE ACTIVATOR IS THE ARM THAT CARRIES THE ITEM. A toast outlives the process that raised it; when somebody presses Review an hour later, Windows COM-activates the LocalServer32 registered for that CLSID. Without it the toast still appears and pressing it does nothing, which is the failure that looks most like success and exactly what a screenshot of a notification would have certified. WHAT THIS CASE DOES NOT SETTLE: that a toast is drawn, and that a press re-activates the app. Both need UserNotificationListener, whose capability is only grantable to a packaged application; DEF-082 carries them and is downstream of DEF-073. The shell's own report that the platform accepted a Show is carried in the evidence as writerSelfReport and is graded by nothing, because a process reporting its own effect is the shape of claim DEF-072 was about.
rows.why: a measurement, not a task: status 'pass' may only be retirable/verified-done. It rolls up to DEF-072, DEF-073, DEF-082.

rows.note: The toast's wire format, on both sides of the trip, checkable with no display. ToastPayloadCodecTests parses the XML the platform will parse - it is a toast, it carries the title and the 'Nothing has been installed' line, it offers exactly Review and Dismiss - and then drives every argument string in that document back through the reader a real click goes through, requiring Review to come back as OpenReviewSheet FOR THAT CAPABILITY. Without the capability travelling, the action is a navigation to a list and the operator has to go and find the item the toast was about. THE SAFETY RULE IS ASSERTED OF THE DOCUMENT RATHER THAN OF ITS OWN SENTENCE. WIN22 tested ToastSafetyRule by asserting the string contained its own words. Here every action's arguments must parse into a closed set of two, and six refusal rows require the reader to return null - not a default - for an empty string, a bare form with no scheme, another application's scheme, our scheme with no action, and an action outside the set. That last row is the one that matters: this process does not control what sits in the Action Center, and a reader that fell back to something that ACTS would be the defect the safety rule names arriving through the parser.

rows.note: A real MSIX, built, deployed and removed, with a recorder at each step that is not the thing that wrote it. MakeAppx packs and .NET's ZipArchive reads the OPC container back - so the identity assertion is made against the PACKED ARTIFACT rather than against the file on disk that was handed to the packer. `winget validate` is the winget client applying a schema this repository does not own. Add-AppxPackage deploys and Get-AppxPackage reports: Fledgeling.MCPRouter_0.1.0.0_x64__facmrsw33693e. THE INSTALL ARM IS WHAT TURNS A FILE INTO A PACKAGE. A manifest can pack cleanly, validate cleanly, and be refused at deployment for a capability, an architecture or a signature - and every static check in the world passes right up to that point. 'CLEAN UNINSTALL RULES' IS THE HALF WORTH READING TWICE. UninstallGuidance promises that uninstalling preserves %USERPROFILE%\.claude\mcp-router. That is a promise about what SURVIVES, and a promise about survival cannot be checked by any amount of reading - only by an uninstall that actually ran. The lane plants a marker, installs, removes, and requires both that the deployment stack reports the package gone and that the marker is still there. WHAT THE LANE PUTS BACK: a self-signed certificate is added to LocalMachine\TrustedPeople so an unsigned developer package can deploy at all, and removed in a finally block however the run ends. Verified afterwards: zero Fledgeling.* packages, zero witness certificates. A lane that left a trusted publisher behind would have changed what this machine will install, silently and for every future run. NOT SETTLED: that anyone can obtain the package. Nothing publishes it, the winget InstallerUrl is a deliberate example.invalid placeholder, and this lane asserts the placeholder is PRESENT so the manifest cannot be mistaken for a shipping one. DEF-083 carries the publishing step, which needs a signing certificate and a pull request into a third-party repository.

rows.note: R26. An expiry needs no probe at all, so this feature arms no task, holds no timer and spawns nothing — which is why it is ON by default where health probing is off. The vacuity rule is `warnWithinMs`'s floor of 60000 with zero REFUSED: at zero a token passes straight from valid to expired, `expiring` is unreachable, and the promise 'you are told before it stops working' would hold only because nothing can enter the state it names.
